text:
alex: pager duty firing — several infer-usw nodes transitioning NotReady around 10:00 UTC, high QPS struggling. seeing OOMKilled in runtime pods on nodes 10.12.4.5/6, and kubelet restarts. paging now.
pd-bot: PD alert created: Inference Pool (infer-usw) node flapping leading to degraded capacity — Sev2.
alex: quick check — kubectl get nodes shows 3x NotReady in infer-usw-az1 pool. logs show kubelet restart loops: 
alex: ```journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 | tail -n 80
Mar 15 09:58:12 node-10-12-4-5 kubelet[1234]: E0315 09:58:12 kubelet.go:... runtime service not responding
Mar 15 09:58:13 node-10-12-4-5 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 15 09:58:14 node-10-12-4-5 kubelet[1234]: Container runtime failed to start container: Error response from daemon: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = containerd: container \"...\" OOMKilled
```
maya: acked, joining. I'm seeing spikes in p95 latency on the inference route and tail errors in the runtime: "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS" and repeated driver resets. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/infer-usw/p99
sarah: I can confirm customer-facing error rate increased. A small subset of requests ~1.2% are returning 5xx and we have queued waiting requests. Start triage steps: 1) isolate bad nodes, 2) shift traffic to fallback pool, 3) reduce runtime batch sizes and lower memory footprint.
james: agree. I'm prepping a cordon/drain on the immediate flapping nodes to stop scheduling. Will not drain pods with local storage until we can evict gracefully.
james: `kubectl cordon node-10-12-4-5`
ops-bot: node node-10-12-4-5 cordoned by james.
alex: also bumping Dedicated fallback pool (infer-usw-fallback) capacity +2 replicas via autoscaler override. maya, can you flip the routing policy to prefer fallback and allow regional spill?
maya: on it. Patching routing policy in control plane: `curl -X PATCH https://controlplane.internal/v1/route/infer-usw -d '{"preferred_pools": ["infer-usw-fallback","infer-usw"]}'` -> response 200. Traffic shift initiated.
infra-bot: Routing reconfig acknowledged. New distribution will take ~15s to converge.
sarah: posting a short customer-facing note in #incidents once we have more data. We should mention degraded latency and partial errors with ongoing mitigation.
alex: mitigation ongoing: observed kernel messages show repeated NV driver crashes. hypothesis: driver update or bad kernel/GPU firmware combo causing Xid 79. I'll open a node-level incident to coordinate with infra team if nodes don't stabilize after cordon + drain.
maya: meanwhile reducing model runtime config to decrease per-request memory: `PATCH /v1/runtime/config {"batch_max_tokens": 512, "kv_cache": "partial", "quant_mode": "int8-preference"}` — applied to the noisy model version, lowering batch pooling. This should reduce OOM pressure.
alex: logs after scaling and cordon: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep runtime` shows a few restarts but most requests being handled by fallback pool. p95 latency fell from 650ms to 320ms for the last minute.
james: starting drains for nodes 10.12.4.5 and 10.12.4.6 with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=60`. Monitoring evictions.
ops-bot: drain started for node-10-12-4-5. 40 pods evicted, 6 pending due to local storage.
maya: we should also flip the runtime to use a lower-memory model variant (v2-lite) for any routed requests to fallback pool — I'll add an automatic model fallback flag. `PATCH /v1/models/v2/settings {"serve_variant":"v2-lite"}`
alex: good call. Doing a rolling restart on agent on fallback pool to pick policy. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-agent -n infer-fallback`
sarah: customer update draft: "We're aware of degraded inference performance in US-West. We're investigating a subset of GPU nodes experiencing driver/kernel issues. We've shifted traffic to fallback capacity and implemented temporary runtime config changes to reduce memory pressure. We'll post updates every 30 minutes." Approve? :eyes:
alex: approve, post it.
sarah: posted to #incidents and emailed CSMs.
pd-bot: PD note — oncall handoff scheduled in 28 minutes.
maya: I'm going to try a soft restart of kubelet on node-10.12.4-6 to see if driver recovers: `ssh root@10.12.4.6 'systemctl restart kubelet'` — do we want that or proceed with full reprovision?
james: do the soft restart first, less blast radius. If it comes back healthy, we can uncordon.
alex: agree. Also gather `dmesg` and GPU driver logs into /var/log/collects/infer-usw/ for infra. `scp root@10.12.4-6:/var/log/nvidia* /mnt/collects/`
maya: kubelet restart issued. watching node.
ops-bot: kubelet restart on node-10-12-4-6 completed. Node changed to Ready -> NotReady -> Ready in ~90s then NotReady again. Behavior indicates kernel-level flakiness.
sarah: customer impact still present but lowered to 0.4% errors after routing shift. Not zero but much better. posting update.
alex: ok, next step — isolate the faulty NIC/kernel combo by removing these nodes from the pool and flag for reprovision. I'm going to create a reprovision ticket with infra and attach logs.
alex: `gh issue create --title "reprovision infer-usw node-10-12-4-x due to GPU Xid 79/kernel panic" --body "attach logs: /var/log/collects/infer-usw/*" --label infra,priority:high`
maya: routing stable after 2 minutes, fallback pool handling 18% extra traffic, autoscaler override still +2, will start ramp-down after 20m if healthy.
james: nodes 10.12.4.5 and .6 marked reprovision. I'm kicking off a rolling replacement in the fleet: `fleetctl reprovision --node node-10-12-4-5,node-10-12-4-6 --reason "gpu driver/kernel instability"`
infra-bot: reprovision ticket created INC-4892, assigned to infra-os-maintainers. Logs uploaded: s3://collects/infer-usw/1765439876-logs.tgz
alex: handoff incoming — my pager window ends in 25m. Maya, do you want to take the remainder of the incident if things are stable?
maya: I can take it. I'll stay on the thread and continue to monitor for the next hour. Alex, if anything spikes >1% error, wake me.
alex: handoff notes: fallback pool handling load, autoscaler override +2, cordoned nodes reprovisioned, model runtime downgraded to v2-lite for fallback, reduced batch_size. Docs/links: dashboard: https://dash.redwood/infer-usw, repro ticket: https://infra.redwood/tickets/INC-4892, routing patch: https://controlplane.internal/changes/8421.
pd-bot: on-call handover: alex -> maya at 1765439906.
ops-bot: autoscaler override applied by alex.
maya: I'll keep alerts muted for non-critical noise and watch the p95 and 5xx. Starting a 30m checkloop: check every 5m p95/p99, check node health, check driver Xid counts.
sarah: I'll keep customer comms in the loop and prepare a postmortem stub. Please annotate approximate timeline and actions.
james: noted: 09:58 — first NotReady, 10:02 — cordon and route shift, 10:05 — runtime config lowered, 10:08 — kubelet restart attempt, 10:15 — reprovision ticket created. Add any extra when incident resolved.
maya: small regression at 10:18 — one more node showed transient NotReady but recovered thanks to routing. Overall error rate steady ~0.3%.
alex: thanks all. I'll log off. Maya—ping me if it climbs.
maya: will do. leaving the thread as incident owner.
ops-bot: Incident resolved? No — monitoring continues. Next update scheduled in 20 minutes.
sarah: created postmortem skeleton: https://docs.redwood/incidents/1765439876 — assign owners for infra and runtime.
maya: closing loop after 60m check if stable. For now we keep fallback routing and reprovision plan active.
pd-bot: PD alert status: acknowledged -> investigating -> mitigated (partial).
